title: Strongly transcendental element over a reduced subring kills quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $R\subseteq S$ be a subring of a commutative ring, with $R$ and $S$ reduced (no nonzero nilpotent elements). Let $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strongly-transcendental] (for the inclusion $R\to S$), and assume that $S$ is a finitely generated module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] over the subring $R[x]\subseteq S$ generated by $R$ and $x$ (so $R\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]). Then $R\to S$ is not quasi-finite at any prime ideal of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00Q2 (lemma-reduced-strongly-transcendental-not-quasi-finite, line 30714; its proof uses Lemmas 00Q0, 00Q1, 00PN)

proof.text: Derive finite type over R by Algebra.FiniteType.trans, since R[x] is generated by x and S is finite over R[x]. Factor polynomial evaluation R[X] -> S through R[x] = (Polynomial.aeval x).range. The codomain-restricted evaluation is surjective: every element of R[x] has a polynomial preimage. Its map is finite by RingHom.Finite.of_surjective; the inclusion R[x] -> S is finite by the hypothesis and RingHom.finite_algebraMap. RingHom.Finite.comp proves that (Polynomial.aeval x).toRingHom is finite.

Suppose IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime R S q. Let p = q.comap (algebraMap R S) and e = PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber R S p, the fibre-prime homeomorphism. The hypothesis is openness of {e <q,rfl>}. Rewrite through Set.image_singleton and e.isOpen_image to obtain openness of {<q,rfl>} in the set-theoretic fibre. Apply Mathlib Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_isOpen_singleton_fiber to obtain Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q.asIdeal. This proves the predicate bridge in Lean rather than assuming agreement of the definitions.

Apply the existing Mathlib candidate Algebra.not_isStronglyTranscendental_of_quasiFiniteAt (Mathlib.RingTheory.ZariskisMainTheorem, line 449, Stacks Tag 00Q2), with the finite evaluation map from step 1 and the quasi-finiteness instance from step 2. It contradicts hx : IsStronglyTranscendental R x. Mathlib has already proved the reduced-ring/minimal-prime argument; no call to the project domain-case or four-rings theorem is needed. All original hypotheses and the conclusion are retained.
